name: crewroom
label: Crew Room
tagline: Claude sessions and Jan at work, pixel-style

manifest.summary: A living anime pixel-art room (Office, Spaceship bridge, Beach, Relaxed room) where every live Claude session is a character at a station, crew helpers sit beside their commander colour-coded by type, and each loaded Jan model is a glowing spirit that grows busier with its CPU use. Click any character for its task, claimed files, recent actions and token use.

features.name: Live sessions
features.description: Reads ~/.claude/sessions/*.json and the tail of each transcript for model, effort, latest tool action and token averages. Read-only.

features.name: Crew helpers
features.description: Background helpers from each session's subagents folder, typed by ~/.claude/agents/*.md frontmatter (model and effort).

features.name: Crew board
features.description: ~/.claude/crew/*/board.json tasks, claims and log shown on the room's board, with claimed files as items on the owner's desk.

features.name: Jan models
features.description: One character per running llama-server model process, glow and bob speed from its CPU share. Process info only; Jan is never queried or restarted.

features.name: Rooms as data
features.description: Rooms are JSON files in ~/ForgeArtData/packs/crewroom/rooms/, sprites are the crewroom packs PixelForge edits. Missing files are seeded from the app's seed/ folder; existing ones are never overwritten.

features.name: New session
features.description: Opens claude in GNOME Terminal in a chosen folder, or starts a headless background task (claude -p, auto mode, prompt on stdin) whose character shows while it runs. The only part of the app that writes; posts from other pages are refused.

features.name: Conversation and where
features.description: The details panel reads a session's whole conversation backwards in 256 KB pages (prompts, replies, tool calls in plain words, results by size) and shows where it runs: folder, terminal device and program, name, start time, and a resume command once it has ended.

manifest.data_dir: ~/ForgeArtData (crewroom-* packs, crewroom palette, packs/crewroom/rooms/*.json); background tasks in ~/.local/share/forge/crewroom/tasks/; reads ~/.claude and /proc
known_gaps: Background task permission mode is disputed: this build uses auto (Emerson's answer here), another session reports he said bypass. One constant, launch.MODE.
claude -p reported permissionMode default in its init event despite --permission-mode auto; not yet checked with a task that edits.
A terminal session in a brand-new folder shows no character until the folder-trust question is answered.
Not yet seen with a real crew helper; only the sample crew and fixture tests exercise that.
Helpers crowd their commander's desk when there are three or more.
Token averages come from the last 64 KB of a transcript and can cover only a few replies.
improvements: Settle the background permission mode with Emerson, then run one task that edits a file to see which mode applies.
Tell the person to answer the trust question when a terminal opens in a new folder.
Keep open result toggles and tool labels when Load earlier re-renders the conversation.
Watch a real crew once, because helper walking and reporting are only fixture-tested.
Spread helpers along a row or a bench so they stop overlapping.
Keep a per-session running token average in memory between polls.
Art polish in PixelForge: palm leaves, side-walk frames, helper side views.
